name: Design a Time-Blocked Daily Schedule and Energy Optimization Plan
prompt:
Design an optimized daily schedule for the person described below. Save the schedule to daily_schedule.json.

Person profile:
- Name: Alex
- Work hours: 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM (9 hours)
- Self-reported peak energy: 9:00 AM - 12:00 PM (high), 12:00 PM - 2:00 PM (low, post-lunch), 2:00 PM - 4:00 PM (medium), 4:00 PM - 6:00 PM (low-medium)
- Must-do tasks today:
  * Write technical specification for new API (estimated 2 hours, high cognitive load)
  * Three 30-minute 1:1 meetings (can be scheduled any time)
  * Code review for 2 pull requests (estimated 1 hour, medium cognitive load)
  * Reply to all pending emails and Slack messages (estimated 45 minutes, low cognitive load)
  * Fix a known bug with a 4 PM deployment deadline (estimated 1.5 hours, high cognitive load)

daily_schedule.json must have exactly this structure:
{
  "person": "Alex",
  "date": "2026-04-11",
  "time_blocks": [
    { "start": "HH:MM", "end": "HH:MM", "task": "<task name>", "energy_level": "high|medium|low", "cognitive_load": "high|medium|low" }
  ],
  "energy_alignment_score": <integer 0-10>,
  "productivity_notes": ["<note 1>", "<note 2>"]
}

Requirements:
- date must be "2026-04-11"
- time_blocks must cover the full 9:00-18:00 window without gaps or overlaps
- All 5 task types must appear in time_blocks
- The bug fix task must end by 16:00 (4 PM)
- High cognitive load tasks must be scheduled only in high or medium energy blocks (not in the 12:00-14:00 low-energy window)
- energy_alignment_score must be an integer 0-10
- productivity_notes must have at least 2 entries

criteria.description: daily_schedule.json file is present in the working directory.
daily_schedule.json parses as valid JSON without errors.
Top-level object contains person, date, time_blocks, energy_alignment_score, and productivity_notes fields.
Each time block has start, end, task, energy_level, and cognitive_load fields.
All energy_level and cognitive_load values are one of: high, medium, or low.
All time blocks whose task contains "bug" or "fix" have an end time at or before 16:00.
energy_alignment_score is an integer between 0 and 10.
criteria.testPattern: energy_alignment_score is an integer between 0 and 10

criteria.description: productivity_notes array has at least 2 non-empty strings longer than 5 characters.

eval.rubric:
Context: The agent designed a time-blocked schedule matching task cognitive load to energy levels.

Criterion 1: Schedule Optimization Quality (Weight: 60%)
1.0: Technical spec and bug fix are scheduled during 9-12 or 14-16 energy windows; meetings and email are in low-energy slots (post-lunch or late afternoon); schedule flows logically with no obvious inefficiencies.
0.5: Most high-load tasks are in good slots but one is placed sub-optimally.
0: High-load tasks are scheduled during the post-lunch low-energy window.

Criterion 2: Productivity Notes Quality (Weight: 40%)
1.0: Notes contain specific, actionable insights about Alex's schedule (e.g., why the spec was placed in the morning, how to protect deep work time, what to do during the post-lunch dip), not generic tips.
0.5: Notes are present but generic rather than tailored to Alex's specific profile.
0: Notes are missing or are single-word entries.
eval.name: Quality Judge
